data.title: Claude Instructions, Projects, Skills, Connectors, Chats

pieces.name: Custom instructions
pieces.plain: Tell Claude once how you like things. It applies to every chat.
pieces.like: A note on the fridge for a new housemate.
setup: Open your settings and find your preferences
Write them in plain words: tone, length, words to avoid
Keep it short: it's read in every chat
pieces.best: Plain English, short answers, words you never want to see.
pieces.mistake: Pasting one job's steps in here. Don't write "Always format reports like this." Write "Keep answers short."

pieces.name: Projects
pieces.plain: A space for one piece of work, with its files behind every chat.
pieces.like: The folder you hand a new colleague for one client.
setup: Create a project for one client or course
Add the files Claude should read
Start your chats inside the project
pieces.best: One client, one course, one big piece of work with lots of files.
pieces.mistake: Expecting it in other chats. It only works inside that project. Open the project first.

pieces.name: Skills
pieces.plain: One job, done your way. Used only when a request needs it.
pieces.like: A recipe card, pulled out only when that dish is ordered.
setup: Name it in a request to be sure
pieces.best: The job you've explained to Claude three times.
pieces.mistake: Three jobs in one skill. Don't make "my-work". Make "weekly-report".

pieces.name: Connectors
pieces.plain: Let Claude into your other apps: your drive, your calendar.
pieces.like: A spare set of keys you give someone you trust.
pieces.best: Answers that live somewhere else: the latest doc, today's meetings.
pieces.mistake: Thinking access teaches Claude how you work. A connector reaches your tracker. A skill teaches how your team writes tickets.

pieces.name: Just ask
pieces.plain: A one-off job? Ask in a normal chat. No setup at all.
pieces.like: Asking a colleague a quick question at their desk.
setup: Explain the job in the chat
Explained it three times? Make a skill
pieces.best: Jobs you'll only do once or twice.
pieces.mistake: Building a skill too early. Don't automate a job you haven't done three times yet.

post:
Don't open Claude again until you've read this:

(then forward it to your whole team)

> first, the one switch skills need
> settings → capabilities → "Create and edit files"
> on Team plans, skills are on by default
> on Enterprise? an owner has to turn them on first
> then know this: Claude remembers how you work in 5 places

CUSTOM INSTRUCTIONS (the note on the fridge)
> how you like things, in every single chat
> plain English, short answers, words you never want to see
> start with: "Write in plain English. Keep answers short. Ask me before you assume anything about my work."
> never paste one job's steps in here. they follow you everywhere

PROJECTS (the folder for one client)
> one space per client, course or big piece of work
> add the files once. every chat inside the project can read them
> try: "Using the files here, summarise what changed this month."
> it only works inside that project. open the project first

SKILLS (the recipe card)
> one job, done your way, in any chat
> Claude reads a one-line description to decide when to use it
> install: Customize → Skills → + → Create skill → Upload a skill
> upload the zip as it is. don't unzip it
> to be sure, name it: "Use my weekly-report skill on these notes."
> one skill, one job. not "my-work". "weekly-report"

CONNECTORS (the spare keys)
> let Claude into your other apps: your drive, your calendar
> use them when the answer lives somewhere else
> access isn't instruction. a connector reaches your files
> it doesn't teach Claude how you like the work done

JUST ASK (the quick question)
> a one-off job? no setup. explain it in the chat
> save the prompt you liked, in case it comes back
> explained it 3 times? now it's a skill

BONUS: stack them
> the connector reaches your project tracker
> the skill knows how your team writes tickets
> the project holds the background
> your instructions keep it all in plain English
> which one goes where, in 2 questions: https://mojeedabisiga.com/learn/guides/skill-or-something-else/

I could tell you Claude takes months to learn. It doesn't.
I could tell you you're already too late. You're not.
I could tell you there's a secret setup. And sell it to you.

But I won't.

Your time matters. You have real work to do.
AI gets simpler every month, not harder.

You just need to put each thing in the right drawer.

And if you want the step-by-step, I keep every guide free: https://mojeedabisiga.com/learn
